missing: Compartment-specific rates for P4->IHH, LIF->STAT3 and decidualization->mechanical permissiveness.
impact: Absolute MaBoSS time and transition rates are weakly identifiable.
proposed_resolution: Time-course pSTAT3/IHH/BMP2/HAND2 and matched adhesion imaging in ADOC.

missing: True human embryo adhesion concentration-response for HBEGF, SPP1, CD98, CDH1, PODXL, PCSK5 and ANXA2.
impact: Cannot assign quantitative rate modifiers confidently.
proposed_resolution: Common-dose perturbation panel with the same adhesion endpoints and toxicity controls.

missing: Several integrin, WNT and ligand mechanisms execute partly on trophectoderm.
impact: Risk of putting embryo biology inside maternal cells.
proposed_resolution: Use external inputs now; add trophoblast only with identifiable embryo data in PhysiBoSS2.

missing: Surface abundance, glycosylation and spatial clearance are not equivalent.
impact: Single-node MUC1 rules can reverse the biological interpretation.
proposed_resolution: Measure glycoforms/sLeX and abundance separately; retain dual nodes.

missing: Donor-specific AFM/hydrogel stiffness linked directly to human blastocyst adhesion is sparse.
proposed_resolution: Paired AFM, stromal state profiling and adhesion assays across donors.

impact: Cannot justify direction or thresholds in MaBoSS.
proposed_resolution: Small factorial perturbation around physiological ranges with viability/barrier counter-readouts.

missing: Many perturbations affect junctions, viability or morphology nonspecifically.
impact: False anti-adhesion hits may simply damage epithelium.
proposed_resolution: Always pair adhesion with TEER/permeability, viability and reversibility endpoints.

missing: Current human embryo sample sizes and donor matching are limited.
impact: Network may overfit a pooled average.
proposed_resolution: At least three donors with matched conditions; hierarchical uncertainty and leave-one-donor-out predictions.

missing: Receptivity marker associations do not imply clinical predictive performance.
impact: Risk of interpreting PAEP/PRL/IGFBP1 or any single marker as implantation outcome.
proposed_resolution: Use markers as internal state observables only; validate stable adhesion separately.

missing: Human, compartment-resolved test of whether HAND2 restrains more than FGF9, and whether any stromal FGF drives HUMAN epithelial proliferation.
impact: S_FGF_MITOGENIC is an aggregate of Fgf1, Fgf2, Fgf9 and Fgf18 taken from one mouse knockout (REF-028); the only human paper (REF-062) finds ONLY FGF9 progestin-regulated and never touches epithelium, so the aggregate does not transfer as an aggregate and LE093 has no human support at all.
proposed_resolution: HAND2 knockdown in primary human ESC with a full FGF panel at protein level, followed by conditioned-medium or recombinant single-FGF challenge of human endometrial epithelium with a proliferation readout and FGFR blockade.

topic: MUC1 abundance versus glycoform at the human luminal surface
missing: A perturbation, in human luminal epithelium, that separates MUC1 abundance, sialylation or keratan-sulphation, and apical clearance, with a matched adhesion endpoint.
impact: REF-067 shows the human luminal MUC1 core protein PERSISTS at receptivity while only an ectodomain epitope is masked, and REF-068 shows progesterone RAISING epithelial MUC1 - both contradict LE013 as a single-abundance rule (see CIT-036, CIT-037). The dual-node design GAP-004 already prescribes is not yet implemented, so one Boolean node currently carries two incompatible readings.
proposed_resolution: Paired glycoform-specific and core-protein detection on the same human luminal epithelium across the cycle, plus enzymatic deglycosylation or ST6GALNAC1/ST3GAL modulation with a blastocyst or spheroid attachment endpoint.

topic: Hormonal context of epithelial PGF2alpha output
missing: PGF2alpha output from primary human glandular epithelium measured under progestin, with and without hCG, in one experiment.
impact: REF-069 (Schatz 1986) reports progesterone INHIBITING endometrial PGF2alpha output and estradiol raising it only in glandular epithelium, while REF-059 (Jin 2025) routes hCG through epithelial PGF2alpha to a stromal decidual readout under db-cAMP plus MPA - i.e. asserts the route in the hormonal context the older paper says suppresses the source. Neither paper can settle it: different cells (primary and organ culture versus Ishikawa), different stimulus, and nearly four decades of assay change. No edge is affected because neither reference is cited by any relation.
proposed_resolution: Primary human glandular epithelial cultures, factorial progestin by hCG, PGF2alpha by a modern immunoassay or LC-MS with a COX inhibitor control arm and PTGFR blockade, read alongside AKR1C3.

missing: An agreed, functionally anchored definition of the epithelial receptive state that does not depend on proliferation direction.
impact: REF-070 treats INCREASED epithelial proliferation as improved receptivity, while REF-028 and the encoded rule LE095 treat termination of epithelial proliferation as a prerequisite. The model can only hold one sign, and marker-based definitions (GAP-009) cannot arbitrate because neither paper measures attachment.
proposed_resolution: Matched human epithelial preparations with proliferation, marker and BLASTOCYST or blastoid attachment endpoints measured in the same wells across a proliferation-modulating perturbation series.

topic: Hedgehog reception in human endometrial stroma
missing: Human evidence that Hedgehog RECEPTION through PTCH1/SMO/GLI is REQUIRED for stromal NR2F2 or HAND2 induction -- a NECESSITY test. What is NOT missing, and must not be requested again: human compartment-resolved expression AND pharmacological response. REF-075 (Wei 2010, JCEM) measures IHH, PTCH1, SMO, GLI1 and GLI2 separately in human endometrial epithelium and stroma across the cycle, and shows the selective PR modulator CDB-2914 raising IHH 5.2-fold and GLI1 3.6-fold in vivo. GLI1 is the canonical pathway-ACTIVITY readout, so human Hedgehog OUTPUT is already known to be progestin-responsive.
impact: The E_IHH -> S_NR2F2 -> S_BMP2 relay is structurally vacuous (E_IHH = E_PGR = S_PGR = S_NR2F2), so any repair needs a determinant at the reception step. REF-075 gives human support for the relay's UPSTREAM half (PR drives IHH and GLI1) and none for the reception step's NECESSITY, which is the determinant actually required. Blocks any S_HH_RECEPTION candidate node.
proposed_resolution: An SMO antagonist, or PTCH1/GLI knockdown, in human endometrial stroma, read out on NR2F2 or HAND2. In ADOC the tractable version is a PTCH1/GLI1 pathway-activity readout in the stromal channel, optionally with an SMO-antagonist arm. Note NR2F2/COUP-TFII was NOT among REF-075's measured targets, so even the correlative human link from Hedgehog output to NR2F2 is untested. Recorded so that expression or pharmacological response is never mistaken for the necessity test.
